target_claim: Claim 1 (solution lines 0043-0044): H is 3-colorable if and only if there exists a valid crossing sequence for the constructed instance, where the construction (lines 0029-0035) sets n=3m with three copies v(1),v(2),v(3) per vertex of H, EG = {(u(i),v(j)) : (u,v) in EH, i=j} union {(v(i),v(j)) : v in VH, i != j}, and k=m+1.
failing_input: H = K1: m = 1, VH = {v0}, EH = {} (also every other H tested: K2/m=2 with EH={(0,1)}, all 3-colorable graphs on m<=4). Constructed instance: n = 3, k = 2, V(G) = {v0(1), v0(2), v0(3)}, E(G) = {(v0(1),v0(2)), (v0(1),v0(3)), (v0(2),v0(3))}.
observed_vs_claimed: Claimed (forward direction of Claim 1): every 3-colorable H maps to a feasible river-crossing instance. Observed: an exhaustive BFS oracle over the full state space (all (L,R,c), 2*2^n states) using the solution's own validity and transition rules (lines 0015-0026) reports crossable = False for H = K1, which is trivially 3-colorable. In fact the initial state has ZERO legal first moves: the three copies of each vertex form a triangle in G, so the unattended left bank may retain at most one copy per vertex, forcing |S| >= 2m for a legal first trip, while capacity permits only |S| <= k-1 = m. The exhaustive sweep over all 75 labelled graphs H on m = 1..4 (n = 3m <= 12) found 74 mismatches; the single agreeing case is K4, which is neither 3-colorable nor crossable, so it agrees vacuously. The constructed instance is infeasible for EVERY H, hence the reduction maps YES-instances of 3-Coloring to NO-instances and establishes nothing. Replaying the solution's own schedule (lines 0054-0063) confirms the error independently: step 1 already lands in an unsafe state (the paper's assertion that 'the remaining passengers C2 union C3 on the left form an independent set' is false, since v(2) and v(3) are enemies by the construction's own edge set), and even if the steps were legal the schedule ships only |C1|+|C2|+|C3| = m of the 3m passengers, never reaching the goal state.
faithfulness_notes: The reduction and the state machine were implemented verbatim from the solution text: vertex set {v(i)}, both edge families exactly as written on line 0034, n = 3m (line 0030), k = m+1 (line 0035), initial/goal states from lines 0018-0019, the validity rule 'the bank Charon is not on must be independent' from lines 0020-0023, and the transition rule 'ship any S subset of Charon's bank with |S| <= k-1' from lines 0024-0026. Nothing was repaired or invented. The oracles are exhaustive: BFS over the entire state space for feasibility and full 3^m enumeration for 3-colorability. All arithmetic is exact (integers, bitmasks, set operations); no floats, no randomness, no wall-clock timing, so the run is deterministic. The one modelling choice not fixed by the text is whether a trip may carry S = {} (Charon crossing alone); the implementation permits it, matching the solution's own step-2/step-4 'Charon returns alone', and this choice only enlarges the move set, so it can only make feasibility easier -- the infeasibility verdict is therefore robust to it.
